_about.purpose: Frozen eval fixture for core/non-core document classification. This file IS the definition of correct; prose rationale lives in the library repo at openspec/work/noncore-content-classification/issues/02-taxonomy-and-unit.md.
_about.unit: spine document (chapter_href) — one keep/drop verdict each

rules.1_informational_value: Drop only if the text has no standalone informational value: a pointer into the physical book (page numbers, 'see X'), or a bare answer/label list whose substance lives elsewhere. Keep anything that explains, defines, derives, or tabulates actual data.
rules.2_front_matter_position: Publisher/apparatus front matter drops even when it is subject-relevant prose. This rule DELIBERATELY CONTRADICTS rule 1 and overrides it — do not 'fix' the inconsistency without re-deciding it. Sampled prefaces genuinely do describe book scope and audience.

scoring: Report precision on the 'drop' class separately from recall — a false positive destroys real content, a false negative only leaves junk behind.
Split rule_1 from rule_2 scores. Rule 2 is a keyword list and should score ~1.0 trivially; rule 1 is the hard judgment. A blended number lets rule 2 mask rule 1.
_about.known_bias: Cases are drawn from 8 equations/code-heavy technical books (TAOCP v1, Algorithms 4e, Applied Statistics for Engineers, Computational Mathematics 2e, Essential Mathematics for Games, Grokking Algorithms 2e, Discovering Statistics Using R, Network Algorithmics 2e). NO Packt, O'Reilly, Apress, or No Starch — 62% of the technical corpus by publisher. A good score here is NOT evidence of corpus-wide accuracy until widened.

cases.label: Glossary
cases.text: 2k factorial experiment. A full factorial experiment with k factors and all factors tested at only two levels (settings) each. Bias. An effect that systematically distorts a statistical result.
cases.note: Real definitions. NOTE: 'glossary' currently sits in back_matter_toc_labels and is wrongly dropped — this case is the regression guard for that fix.

cases.label: Appendix A. Performance of AVL trees
cases.text: AVL trees guarantee O(log n) lookup by keeping the height difference between subtrees at most one. The rebalancing operation after an insert requires at most two rotations.
cases.note: CONTRAST WITH bibliography-citations: both labelled 'appendix', opposite verdicts. This is an ordinary technical chapter.
